bw: Secreted by parathyroid chief cells
Released in response to low blood calcium
Stimulates osteoclasts
tp: PTH raises blood calcium by stimulating osteoclasts, increasing renal calcium reabsorption and starting calcitriol production.

ww.Calcitonin: Calcitonin comes from the thyroid and is released when calcium is high.
ww.Calcitriol: Calcitriol is made in the kidney under PTH influence, not secreted by parathyroid chief cells.

evidence: The parathyroid glands produce and secrete PTH, a peptide hormone, in response to low blood calcium levels (Figure 17.16).

bw: Primary functional cells of the parathyroid glands
Secrete PTH
tp: Chief cells make PTH. The function of the oxyphil cells is not clear.

ww.Oxyphil cells: The function of oxyphil cells is not clear; they are not the PTH-secreting cells.
ww.Parafollicular cells: Parafollicular cells are in the thyroid and secrete calcitonin.

evidence: The primary functional cells of the parathyroid glands are the chief cells.

bw: PTH acts on the kidney tubules
Effect on calcium and magnesium in the urine filtrate
tp: PTH keeps calcium in the blood by increasing its reabsorption in the kidney tubules.

ww.Decreases reabsorption of calcium: That would lower blood calcium, the opposite of PTH.
ww.Increases reabsorption of phosphate: PTH does not act to raise blood phosphate; the described effect is on calcium and magnesium.

evidence: PTH causes increased reabsorption of calcium (and magnesium) in the kidney tubules from the urine filtrate.

bw: Active form of vitamin D3
Made in the kidneys when PTH acts
Increases intestinal absorption of dietary calcium
tp: PTH initiates calcitriol (1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D) production in the kidneys, and calcitriol raises calcium absorption in the intestines.

ww.Calcitonin: Calcitonin lowers blood calcium and is made by the thyroid.
ww.Cortisol: Cortisol is an adrenal corticosteroid, not a vitamin D hormone.

evidence: In addition, PTH initiates the production of the steroid hormone calcitriol (also known as 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D), which is the active form of vitamin D3, in the kidneys.

bw: PTH secretion
Stimulates osteoclasts that degrade bone
d: Excretion of calcium in the urine
tp: PTH stimulates osteoclasts and inhibits osteoblasts, which releases calcium into the interstitial fluid and spares blood calcium.

ww.Deposition of calcium into bone: PTH inhibits osteoblasts, the cells that deposit bone.
ww.Excretion of calcium in the urine: PTH increases renal calcium reabsorption, so less is excreted.

evidence: PTH secretion causes the release of calcium from the bones by stimulating osteoclasts, which secrete enzymes that degrade bone and release calcium into the interstitial fluid.

bw: Overproduction of PTH
Excessive calcium reabsorption from bone
Reduced bone density with spontaneous fractures
tp: Excess PTH drains calcium from bone, causing fractures or deformities, while high blood calcium reduces nervous system responsiveness and can deposit in tissues.

ww.Hypoparathyroidism: Hypoparathyroidism is PTH deficiency with low blood calcium.
ww.Hyperthyroidism: Hyperthyroidism is excess thyroid hormone, not excess PTH.

evidence: Abnormally high activity of the parathyroid gland can cause hyperparathyroidism, a disorder caused by an overproduction of PTH that results in excessive calcium reabsorption from bone.

bw: PTH deficiency
May follow injury or surgery involving the thyroid gland
Low blood calcium with muscle cramping and spasms
tp: Low calcium raises sodium permeability of membranes, causing twitching, cramps, spasms and convulsions. Severe deficits can paralyze breathing muscles.

ww.Hyperparathyroidism: Hyperparathyroidism is PTH excess with high blood calcium.
ww.Hypothyroidism: Hypothyroidism is low thyroid hormone with a slow metabolic rate.

evidence: In contrast, abnormally low blood calcium levels may be caused by parathyroid hormone deficiency, called hypoparathyroidism, which may develop following injury or surgery involving the thyroid gland.

bw: Why low blood calcium causes muscle twitching and spasms
tp: Low calcium makes membranes more permeable to sodium, producing muscle twitching, cramping, spasms or convulsions.

ww.Decreased membrane permeability to sodiu: High calcium, not low calcium, decreases sodium permeability.
ww.Decreased nervous system excitability: High calcium reduces nervous responsiveness; low calcium does the opposite.

evidence: Low blood calcium increases membrane permeability to sodium, resulting in muscle twitching, cramping, spasms, or convulsions.

bw: Number of parathyroid glands most people have
tp: Most people have four parathyroid glands embedded in the posterior surface of the thyroid, though more can occur in the neck or chest.

ww.Two: Most people have four, not two.
ww.Six: Most people have four; extra glands are only occasional.

evidence: Most people have four parathyroid glands, but occasionally there are more in tissues of the neck or chest.

bw: Negative feedback on PTH release
What inhibits further PTH secretion
tp: Low calcium stimulates PTH; as calcium rises it inhibits more PTH release.

ww.Rising blood phosphate levels: The feedback described in the source is calcium, not phosphate.

evidence: A negative feedback loop regulates the levels of PTH, with rising blood calcium levels inhibiting further release of PTH.
